title: Concession Simulator: pricing impact model + legal review workflow for MSA/DPA indemnity variations
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Problem: Sales/customer success negotiates MSA/DPA concessions (indemnity caps, liability carve-outs, data residency exceptions) with no quick way to estimate downstream revenue impact or how the change will route through Legal/Security. This causes ad-hoc approvals, longer time-to-sign, and inconsistent pricing outcomes.

Goal: Build a Concession Simulator and legal-review workflow that lets Pricing/AE quickly see an estimated ARR impact and required approval path for a proposed concession, integrates security questionnaire signals, and feeds telemetry into pricing experiments. The simulator will enable A/B-style experiments (e.g., auto-approve low-risk indemnity cap increases for high-volume self-serve deals) and provide concrete metrics for pricing/contracting trade-offs.

Scope: MVP covers common concessions: indemnity cap changes, liability cap exceptions, escrow/escrow alternative requests, subprocessor/data residency exceptions, and standard DPA clause overrides. The feature includes: (1) a scoring model that maps concessions to risk buckets and estimated legal hours; (2) a pricing impact calculator (expected ARR change, list price delta given concession tiers); (3) routing logic to decide auto-approve vs manual Legal review; (4) UI hooks for the sales contract editor and the internal concessions dashboard; (5) telemetry capture for experiment measurement (time-to-sign, legal hours saved, conversion delta).

Non-goals: Full natural language contract ingestion or clause-level automated drafting. This MVP will use a rules+ML hybrid classifier and a curated concession library rather than attempting full redline parsing of arbitrary MSAs.

Why now: Rising enterprise usage and larger custom deals mean concessions materially affect revenue. We need a reproducible way to run pricing experiments tied to contract flexibility and reduce legal cycles for low-risk deviations.

Artifacts: Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Concession+Simulator (WIP); Pricing model notebook (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-example; Github prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/contracts-prototypes/pull/237

Stakeholders: Legal (R. Martinez), Security (Priya Desai), Sales Ops (Ethan Wu), Pricing (Maya Singh), Engineering (runtime & infra leads), Design (Iris Kwan).
acceptance_criteria: Simulator returns a risk score (low|medium|high) and estimated legal hours for any concession in the curated library in <2s for 95% of calls
Pricing impact view shows expected ARR delta and recommended list-price adjustment given concession tier
Routing policy engine implements at least two rulesets: conservative (requires legal approval for medium+) and experimental (auto-approve low, escalate medium)
Sales UI shows a one-click ‘Simulate concession’ action that records the simulation result and the chosen routing decision
Telemetry events (concession_simulation.request, concession_simulation.result, concession_approval.decision) are emitted to analytics with stable schema
Run a 4-week pilot with three AE teams and capture time-to-sign, legal hours expended, and closed-won delta versus control
Security questionnaire integration returns flagged controls (true/false) for questions relevant to concessions and influences routing decision
